messages:
maria: Quick sync — want to lock down how we handle null vs absent in the obs proto. We've seen ingestion surprises when SDKs start sending empty strings vs omitting fields.
kevin: +1. Can we prefer absent over explicit null to keep payloads small? But we need a plan for consumers that expect presence.
sara: In practice some downstream joins rely on the attribute existing even if empty. If we switch to absent we might break lookups.
maria: Right. Options I sketched: (1) keep fields required and use empty-string sentinel; (2) make fields optional and treat missing as unknown; (3) add explicit presence bitmask in envelope. Tradeoffs?
tomas: (3) sounds heavy. It couples everyone to a new envelope bitfield. (2) is clean but forces consumers to tolerate missing keys.
kevin: Concern with (2) is billing attribution — missing billing_key vs empty string changes routing. We need deterministic attribution.
sara: Could we normalize at ingest with a cheap adapter: if billing_key missing -> try lookup via tenant header -> populate pseudo-key and tag with _inferred flag. That keeps SDKs free to omit.
maria: That seems pragmatic. Ingest-time enrichment + a provenance tag. Downstreams can opt out if they require rawness.
kevin: How about versioning? If we change nullability rules we must bump proto major or at least a schema version in the envelope. We can't silently change semantics.
tomas: Add a small schema_version int to the envelope metadata. Ingest adapters can switch behavior based on that. No need for full major proto churn.
proto-lint-bot: lint: new-field "schema_version" recommended at envelope.level (int32).
sara: If we add schema_version, we should document migration policy: >=X means missing billing_key allowed and will be enriched; <X means expect billing_key present.
maria: Agreed. Migration plan: 1) publish RFC + proto patch 2) SDKs ship shim that continues to set billing_key for one release 3) 2-week opt-in where ingesters infer and add _inferred flags 4) >=cutover version remove requirement.
kevin: Rolling timeline seems fair. Also add telemetry counter: ingest.enrichment.inferred_billing_key{yes/no} so we can measure blast radius.
sara: We should also store original raw envelope (or diff) for compliance for a short window in case accounting needs original value. Maybe a 7-day retention of raw diffs.
tomas: Impl note: enrichment should be idempotent and deterministic. If we infer from headers, ensure canonicalization of header case and tenant aliases.
maria: Good call. I'll draft the proto patch snippet — propose adding: 
```
message Envelope {
  int32 schema_version = 1;
  map<string,string> attrs = 2;
  repeated string path = 3;
  // new provenance flags
  bool enrichment_inferred = 10;
}
```
kevin: For attrs map, call out which keys must be preserved vs allowed to be normalized (billing_key, tenant_id, sample_rate).
sara: Add a per-key provenance map? e.g., attrs_provenance: map<string,string> where value in {"raw","inferred","normalized"}. Lightweight strings ok.
tomas: That helps downstream query behavior. But increases payload. Maybe compress provenance into a single bitset per well-known key and keep it opt-in.
maria: Let's iterate in the RFC. Action items: maria write RFC + proto diff, kevin run a quick cost calc for provenance payload size, sara define the enrichment heuristics and required lookups, tomas prototype idempotent adapter. We'll plan a short demo in next Thurs sync.
kevin: I'll also add metrics and a tiny dashboard to watch inferred vs raw billing attribution.
sara: 👍 and I can draft SDK guidance: "Prefer omitting non-required attrs; if you send empty string it will be treated as present".
maria: Thanks — i'll send RFC link when done. :thumbsup:
